title: 材料科学Ⅲ
subtitle: Materials Science III
educationalGoal: In the design and manufacture of machines and structures, it is necessary to select appropriate materials based on an understanding of their properties. Based on the basic knowledge of the structure and properties of materials acquired in Materials Science I and II, students learn corrosion and fracture mechanisms, which are defects of materials, and understand the structure and properties of nonferrous metals, resins, ceramics, and composite materials. Furthermore, students discuss some cases of material selection and it helps deeper understanding of materials.
advice:
The following items are studied.
-Corrosion and corrosion protection techniques
-Fracture mechanics
-Stainless steel and alloyed steel
-Aluminum and aluminum alloys
-Copper and copper alloys
-Plastics
-Ceramics
-Composite materials

Some case studies of material selection based on Ishikawa area are discussed in order to understand materials knowledge deeper.

Lectures are conducted by face-to-face teaching, also can be took place by remote class depending on a situation.
requiredKnowledge: This lecture requires the understanding of Materials Science I and Materials Science II. Students should understand the relationship between microstructure and material properties in Materials Science I,and also understand the relationship between microstructure formation and properties of steel in Materials Science Ⅱ. Knowledge of thermodynamics is also required to understand corrosion mechanisms.

activityGoals.body: Abilities to understand the basic mechanisms of corrosion, typical corrosion forms and corrosion control methods
Abilities to understand the failure mechanisms of materials.
Abilities to understand the properties of stainless steel and alloyed steels.
Abilities to understand the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resigns, composite materials.
Abilities to select appropriate materials according to engineering needs.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1) Abilities to understand the basic principle of corrosion and typical corrosion forms, and to select appropriate corrosion protection methods.
2) Abilities to be able to explain the failure mechanism of materials.
3) Abilities to understand the characteristics of alloyed steels and stainless steels.
4)Abilities to be able to explain the relationship between the structure and the properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resins and composite materials.
5)Abilities to be able to select appropriate materials using the knowledge acquired in this course.
achievementLevels.standard:
1) Abilities to understand that corrosion progresses by the anode reaction and cathode reaction and to explain the principle of cathodic protection.
2) Abilities to be able to explain the meaning of the plane strain fracture toughness value (KIC).
3)Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of advanced materials such as alloy steel and stainless steels.
4) Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of typical aluminum and copper alloys, ceramics, resins and composite materials.
5) Abilities to be able to point out the hazards of materials in the environment in which they are used.
